title: Early street parades with the Tuxedo Brass Band
summary: Frazier talks about funeral marches and being started on parades by Trepagnier in the original Tuxedo Brass Band.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You ever play any parades in your early days?
Did they play the same kind of stuff as they played?

It's mostly the same stuff you play in the day. Lots of funeral marches. I'll tell you how the bands did them days. Any band had a funeral march. They'd take the name of it, so the other band wouldn't know the name of it. Yeah, yeah. And the first man that started me on the parade was Ones Trapania, playing the parade. He played the bass drum, and I played the snare drum. That was part of the original tuxedo brass band.

Yeah. Willie Paggio and Ones Trapania and myself. I think they had manual parades out that day. As long as we left a hall they called the New Hall on the street. They called North Durbin Street. It was many years ago. The first man brought me on a street parade.
